text:
pagerbot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired: HIGH error rate on inference-gateway-prod-eu-west1 (5xx). Current window: 5m. Error rate: 18% (threshold 5%). Requests/sec ~420 -> 5xx/sec ~76. Alert ID: PD-ALRT-91234. Link: https://pd.example/alerts/PD-ALRT-91234

pd-bot: Auto-escalation scheduled in 5m if not ACKed. Runbook: https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/inference-5xx-spike

oncall-sre: ACK - I'm on. Looking at grafana now, will grab request logs.

alex: thanks. Maya/Infra - any deploys or config pushes in eu-west overnight? @maya @jordan

maya: nothing from infra since 03:12 UTC. No config pushes. CI shows a webapp deploy to gateway-prod at 02:58 but low traffic then.

jordan: checking autoscaler logs now. Scaling events look normal. Queue depth increased ~2x. Could be upstream model nodes overwhelmed.

oncall-sre: tailing logs:
```
2026-03-14T02:56:10Z ERROR inference-gateway: upstream 502 on /v1/generate id=abc123 host=model-node-17
2026-03-14T02:56:10Z ERROR inference-gateway: upstream 504 on /v1/chat id=def456 host=model-node-9
```

alex: any customer-facing traffic pattern? Large batch jobs?

sam: Not that I can see in traceroutes. Most of the traffic is short chat completions. A few keys from a partner show elevated qps but not enough to explain 18% 5xx.

oncall-sre: quick mitigation idea: enable immediate traffic routing to eu-central1 fallback pool for new requests and keep eu-west for sticky sessions. Can we flip routing?

maya: we can patch the routing policy; I'll open a canary route divert to eu-central with 20% traffic. Deploying policy change now.

pd-bot: PD: escalation to second responder after 2 minutes (auto).

oncall-sre: meanwhile I'm restarting the suspected model node pair (model-node-9/17) via the operator: `kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-runtime --namespace=prod --selector=instance in (9,17)`

jordan: rolling restart triggered. Watching readiness probes.

oncall-sre: after restart, a few 5xxs still happen but rate dropped to ~7% in last 2 minutes. Good sign.

alex: Patch traffic routing worked?

maya: Canary diverted 20% to eu-central; metrics show eu-west 5xx dropping to ~8% and eu-central healthy at ~0.5%. Increasing to 50%?

oncall-sre: hold at 50% for 5m, continue watching. I'll keep logs open for any new upstream errors.

sam: customer impact: we flagged 12k requests failed in the window, mostly short-lived. No major tenant-wide outage reported. Some premium customers saw degraded error rates. Logging a P0? maybe P1 since degraded but partially mitigated. Thoughts?

alex: escalate to P1. Notify CS and account reps for customers with errors >50 errors in window.

oncall-sre: PD status: acknowledged -> in progress. No full page to on-call-manager.

jordan: restarts completed, model-node-9 back to Ready=true. Kernel OOM traces looked empty. Heap usage normal. Not seeing noisy neighbor.

oncall-sre: hypothesis: intermittent networking flaps between gateway and model nodes causing a burst of 502/504. I've opened a ticket with infra to check the vSwitch on host pool.

maya: infra monitoring shows a brief network error burst at 02:55:30Z across hostpool-3, 12s window. We're correlating with host NIC reconfig events. Escalating to hardware ops.

pd-bot: PD: Second responder paged (jordan).

oncall-sre: Jordan, can you validate whether we should failover permanently or keep split routing until hardware is confirmed?

jordan: prefer keep split routing for now until infra confirms. If hardware is flaky we'll failover traffic away from that hostpool entirely.

alex: agree. Also start a postmortem draft and capture timeline. I'll own impact classification and customer comms draft.

oncall-sre: scaling/caching note: enabling KV prefix cache increased hit rate so latency for retried requests improved. Deployed a small cache tweak at 03:10 UTC.

sam: monitoring shows error rate now ~2.1% cluster-wide after routing and restarts. Good.

maya: infra ops confirmed a firmware update got stuck and triggered transient NIC resets on 4 hosts in hostpool-3. They've rolled back the firmware and are re-testing.

oncall-sre: PD: marking incident as under control. Will keep channel open for 30m and then transition to async. Assigning follow-up tickets: INFRA-2219 (hostpool firmware rollback), SRE-3350 (postmortem), CS-4291 (customer outreach).

alex: thanks all. @sam please pull the list of affected customers and send to CS. Jordan/Maya, please add hardware timeline to INFRA-2219.

jordan: ack, updating ticket with timestamps and host ids.

sam: sending affected-customer list now to CS in DM.

pd-bot: PD: Incident PD-ALRT-91234 status changed to resolved by oncall-sre at 03:22 UTC.

oncall-sre: marking thread for handoff: night shift (alex) will pickup follow-ups in morning. Closing live paging.

alex: handoff noted. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:

maya: adding retrospective note to runbook about firmware rollout gating to avoid automatic reboots during high traffic windows.

sam: will file CS follow-up and include suggested customer message.

oncall-sre: closing slack thread; will link postmortem when ready.
